<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Chapter 6 <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Covariant Derivative</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">6.4</span> Torsion and Curvature</h1></header>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p>The <strong>torsion</strong> of a connection <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> is the <span class="math inline">\((1,2)\)</span>-tensor field<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-6" id="fnref-6" aria-label="Footnote 6">6</a></sup>  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathtt{T} : \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} &amp;\longrightarrow C^\infty(\mathcal{M}) \\
            (\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &amp;\longmapsto \mathtt{T}(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq
            \mathsf{X}\left\lceil \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \right\rfloor,
        \end{align*}</span>  where the <strong>commutator</strong> of two vector fields is the vector field  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            [\cdot, \cdot] : \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} &amp;\longrightarrow \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \\
            (\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &amp;\longmapsto [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}], \quad
            [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \coloneqq
            \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil.
        \end{align*}</span>  From now on, whenever a single chart is involved, we drop the chart label, <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma \equiv \Gamma_\mathscr{X}\)</span>. Since <span class="math inline">\([\partial x_j, \partial x_k] = 0\)</span><sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-7" id="fnref-7" aria-label="Footnote 7">7</a></sup>, the components of the torsion read  <span class="math display">\[
            \mathtt{T}^i_{jk} \coloneqq \mathtt{T}(dx^i, \partial x_j, \partial x_k)
            = dx^i\left\lceil \nabla_{\partial x_j} \partial x_k - \nabla_{\partial x_k} \partial x_j \right\rfloor
            = \Gamma^i_{kj} - \Gamma^i_{jk}.
        \]</span></p></li>
<li><p>An affine manifold <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}, \nabla)\)</span> is <strong>torsion free</strong> if <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{T} = 0\)</span>, i.e. if  <span class="math display">\[
            \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} = [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \qquad \forall \, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M},
        \]</span>  which, in any chart, amounts to the symmetry <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma^i_{jk} = \Gamma^i_{kj}\)</span> of the connection coefficient functions. For a torsion-free connection, the normal coordinates constructed above therefore make <em>all</em> the connection coefficient functions vanish at the chosen point <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p>The <strong>Riemann curvature</strong> of a connection <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> is the <span class="math inline">\((1,3)\)</span>-tensor field<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-8" id="fnref-8" aria-label="Footnote 8">8</a></sup>  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathrm{Riem} : \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} \times \Gamma T\mathcal{M} &amp;\longrightarrow C^\infty(\mathcal{M}) \\
            (\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &amp;\longmapsto \mathrm{Riem}(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \\
            &amp;\coloneqq \mathsf{X}\left\lceil \nabla_\mathcal{X} \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Z} - \nabla_{[\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]} \mathcal{Z} \right\rfloor.
        \end{align*}</span>  Its components follow from <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{\partial x_m} \partial x_j = \Gamma^r_{jm} \, \partial x_r\)</span>, the product rule and <span class="math inline">\([\partial x_k, \partial x_m] = 0\)</span>:  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \mathrm{Riem}^i_{jkm}
            &amp;\coloneqq \mathrm{Riem}(dx^i, \partial x_j, \partial x_k, \partial x_m)
            = dx^i\left\lceil \nabla_{\partial x_k} \big( \Gamma^r_{jm} \, \partial x_r \big) - \nabla_{\partial x_m} \big( \Gamma^r_{jk} \, \partial x_r \big) \right\rfloor \\
            &amp;= \partial x_k\left\lfloor \Gamma^i_{jm} \right\rceil - \partial x_m\left\lfloor \Gamma^i_{jk} \right\rceil
            + \Gamma^i_{rk} \, \Gamma^r_{jm} - \Gamma^i_{rm} \, \Gamma^r_{jk}.
        \end{align*}</span>  The Riemann curvature is antisymmetric in its last two indices, <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem}^i_{jkm} = -\mathrm{Riem}^i_{jmk}\)</span>. For a torsion-free connection it satisfies the (differential) <strong>Bianchi identity</strong>  <span class="math display">\[
            (\nabla_\mathcal{W} \mathrm{Riem})(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y})
            + (\nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathrm{Riem})(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{W})
            + (\nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathrm{Riem})(\mathsf{X}, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{W}, \mathcal{X}) = 0,
        \]</span>  for all <span class="math inline">\(\mathsf{X} \in \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\)</span>, or, in components,  <span class="math display">\[
            \big( \nabla_{\partial x_n} \mathrm{Riem} \big)^i_{jkm}
            + \big( \nabla_{\partial x_k} \mathrm{Riem} \big)^i_{jmn}
            + \big( \nabla_{\partial x_m} \mathrm{Riem} \big)^i_{jnk} = 0.
        \]</span></p></li>
<li><p>The <strong>Ricci curvature</strong> of a connection <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> is the <span class="math inline">\((0,2)\)</span>-tensor field obtained by contracting the upper index of the Riemann curvature with its third slot,  <span class="math display">\[
            \mathrm{Ric}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq \mathrm{Riem}(dx^m, \mathcal{X}, \partial x_m, \mathcal{Y}),
        \]</span>  where the sum over <span class="math inline">\(m\)</span> does not depend on the chart employed<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-9" id="fnref-9" aria-label="Footnote 9">9</a></sup>. Its components are <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric}_{ab} \coloneqq \mathrm{Ric}(\partial x_a, \partial x_b) = \mathrm{Riem}^m_{amb}\)</span>. Note that, for a general connection, the Ricci curvature need not be symmetric.</p></li>
</ul>
<div class="dg-footnotes"><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-6"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-6" aria-label="Back to the text">6</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>That the right-hand side is <span class="math inline">\(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>-linear in every argument is not obvious, since <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y}\)</span> alone is not: by the product rule, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_\mathcal{X}(g\,\mathcal{Y}) - \nabla_{g\mathcal{Y}} \mathcal{X} = \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{Y} + g \big( \nabla_\mathcal{X}\mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y}\mathcal{X} \big)\)</span>, while <span class="math inline">\([\mathcal{X}, g\,\mathcal{Y}] = \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{Y} + g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\)</span>, so the non-tensorial terms <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{Y}\)</span> cancel.</p></div></div><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-7"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-7" aria-label="Back to the text">7</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p><span class="math inline">\([\partial x_j, \partial x_k]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil = \Big( \partial_j \partial_k \left[ f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right] - \partial_k \partial_j \left[ f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right] \Big) \circ \mathscr{X} = 0\)</span>, by Schwarz’s theorem.</p></div></div><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-8"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-8" aria-label="Back to the text">8</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>As for the torsion, the non-tensorial terms produced by the product rule cancel, here against those coming from <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_{[\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]} \mathcal{Z}\)</span>.</p></div></div><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-9"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-9" aria-label="Back to the text">9</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>Under a change of chart, the Jacobian factors coming from <span class="math inline">\(dy^m\)</span> and from <span class="math inline">\(\partial y_m\)</span> combine into <span class="math inline">\(\frac{\partial \mathscr{Y}^m}{\partial \mathscr{X}^a} \frac{\partial \mathscr{X}^b}{\partial \mathscr{Y}^m} = \delta^b_a\)</span>.</p></div></div></div>
